classification.difficultyReason: Three labelled polygons must be summed to a perimeter, grouped as a·m + b·n, factorised and matched to the options. This is the same demand as p9-q5, with slightly more sides to count.

content.prompt:
Match the shapes with the expressions that show their perimeters.

A. $2(m+2n)$
B. $2(2m+n)$
C. $2(3m+n)$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P_{\mathrm{i}}&=4m+2n\\P_{\mathrm{i}}&=2(2m+n)\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=2m+4n\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=2(m+2n)\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=6m+2n\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=2(3m+n)\end{align*}$$
The matches are i–B, ii–A and iii–C.
